post.caption: This emerald has a wheel inside. A trapiche emerald shows a pattern like a wheel with six spokes, and it is very rare. The dark arms are mostly carbon, and green emerald fills the gaps between them. The name is Spanish, after the cogwheels used in sugar mills. Almost all come from a few mines in western Colombia, such as Muzo, and a very few have turned up in Brazil and Madagascar. Cutters often polish them into smooth domes called cabochons to show off the six sections. The pattern stays fixed when you tilt the stone, unlike a star effect. Scientists still do not agree on how it forms.
